sentence: She's lived here ___ 2015.
I've been waiting ___ half an hour.
___ you like some more cake?
explanation: 'Would you like…?' is the polite offer; 'Do you like' asks about a general preference.

sentence: There isn't ___ milk left in the fridge.
explanation: In negative sentences use 'any' with uncountable nouns.

sentence: He's the man ___ car was stolen.
explanation: 'whose' shows possession: the man whose car…

sentence: She made me ___ my homework before dinner.
explanation: 'make somebody do' — bare infinitive after the object.

sentence: If I ___ you, I'd apologise immediately.
explanation: 'If I were you' — subjunctive 'were' for unreal situations.

sentence: The bridge ___ built in 1892.
I'd rather ___ at home tonight.
You needn't ___ worried — everything is fine.
___ spite of the traffic, we arrived on time.
She's not as tall ___ her sister.
explanation: 'not as + adjective + as' for negative comparison.

sentence: By the time we arrived, the film ___ already started.
explanation: Past perfect for the earlier of two past events.

sentence: I'm looking forward to ___ you next week.
explanation: 'to' is a preposition here, so -ing follows.

sentence: How ___ bread do we need for the recipe?
There were ___ people at the concert than last year.
He's got a ___ of stamps from every country he's visited.
explanation: Noun form: collection (a group of collected items).

sentence: She denied ___ the money.
___ you mind opening the window?
The train ___ arrive at six, but it's late as usual.
explanation: 'should + infinitive' = what is expected to happen.

sentence: I wish I ___ told him the truth at the time.
explanation: 'wish + past perfect' for regret about the past.

sentence: We'd better ___ going — it's nearly midnight.
I'm not used to ___ such spicy food.
We stopped ___ some photos on the way.
explanation: 'stop to do' = pause in order to do something.

sentence: No sooner had he arrived ___ it started to rain.
I'd rather you ___ smoke in here.
___ from being annoyed, she was delighted.
explanation: 'far from + adjective' = not at all: Far from being annoyed…

sentence: All the tickets ___ sold out by noon.
explanation: Past perfect passive: had been + participle (before the stated past moment).

sentence: She speaks English ___ than her brother.
You ___ have seen a doctor sooner.
explanation: 'should have + participle' criticises a past decision.

sentence: It was ___ a good film that we saw it twice.
I'd like to know when the results ___ be published.
explanation: Future in a noun clause: when the results will be published.

sentence: They insisted ___ paying for everything.
The hotel room wasn't big ___ for three people.
She's the woman ___ helped me find the station.
He must ___ left already — his coat isn't here.
explanation: 'must have + participle' = certain about the past.

sentence: This is the village ___ my grandmother was born.
Do you know how ___ to the station from here?
She's been ___ TV all morning.
explanation: Present perfect continuous for duration up to now: has been watching.

sentence: I'd sooner ___ at home than go to the party.
He apologised for ___ so rude.
___ of my parents speaks French, so I translate for them.
explanation: 'Neither of' = not one and not the other (two people).

sentence: The letters ___ delivered every morning at eight.
It's time we ___ this room a good clean.
He was charged ___ dangerous driving.
I'll call you as soon ___ I land.
We had the walls ___ last month.
explanation: 'have something done' = arrange for it to be done: had the walls painted.

sentence: He told me ___ touch that switch.
I'd rather not ___ about it over the phone.
By this time next year, she ___ finished her degree.
explanation: Future perfect: will have + participle by a future point.

sentence: The thief is believed ___ entered through the roof.
explanation: 'is believed to have + participle' for a past event.

sentence: Unless it ___ , the match will go ahead.
explanation: 'unless' = if…not; present simple after time/condition words.

sentence: She's such ___ interesting person.
explanation: 'such an + adjective + singular noun' — 'interesting' starts with a vowel sound.

sentence: He prefers cycling ___ driving to work.
I'd better not ___ you — you look busy.
She's allergic ___ cats.
We're going to ___ our flight if we don't hurry.
hint: be too late for a plane
explanation: 'miss a flight/train/bus' = arrive too late for it.

sentence: I can't find my glasses ___ .
He ran so fast that we lost ___ of him.
explanation: 'lose sight of somebody' = no longer see them.

sentence: She's very good ___ explaining difficult ideas.
The meeting was put ___ until Thursday.
We arrived ___ Lisbon at dawn.
How long does the flight ___ ?
She's used to ___ long hours.
The parcel ___ yesterday, but we weren't home.
explanation: Past simple for a finished past event.

sentence: He denied ___ the vase, though the camera saw him.
I'd rather walk than ___ the bus.
explanation: 'would rather do A than do B' — both bare infinitives.

sentence: The film is based ___ a true story.
He ___ the flu last week and missed the finals.
explanation: 'catch the flu/a cold' = become ill with it.

sentence: The meeting has been ___ forward to Monday.
explanation: 'bring forward' = move to an earlier time (opposite of put off).

sentence: We're looking ___ to hearing from you.
explanation: 'look forward TO' — the standard closing phrase.

sentence: I couldn't ___ laughing at his accent.
The concert tickets sold ___ in an hour.
He was sacked ___ repeatedly arriving late.
By midnight, everyone ___ gone home.
explanation: Past perfect for the earlier of two past moments.

sentence: The garden is ___ than I expected — it's huge!
You ___ be tired after such a long flight.
explanation: 'must + infinitive' = certain deduction about the present.

sentence: I'll have finished the report ___ Friday.
She's the most generous person I've ___ met.
explanation: 'the best… I've ever seen/met' — 'ever' with superlatives.

sentence: He walked in as ___ nothing had happened.
The meeting was held ___ strict secrecy.
She's been ___ from school three times this term.
explanation: 'be absent from school' — formal way to say not present.

sentence: We ran out ___ petrol on the motorway.
explanation: 'run out OF something' = have none left.

sentence: He's recovering ___ a knee operation.
The new law comes ___ force next month.
explanation: 'come into force' = officially start to apply.

sentence: He was ___ to resign after the scandal.
explanation: 'be forced to do' = be made to do unwillingly.

sentence: We should make the ___ of the good weather.
explanation: 'make the most of' = get the maximum benefit from.

sentence: Her success was largely ___ to her coach.
explanation: 'be down to somebody/something' = be caused by.

sentence: The restaurant is famous ___ its seafood.
He kept ___ even though everyone had left.
It's not worth ___ about the delay now.
The first edition of the book ___ out in 1998.
They had no ___ but to call the police.
The demonstrators were ___ from entering the building.
explanation: 'prevent somebody FROM doing' — passive: were prevented from entering.

sentence: She went to university ___ study law.
The cat cleans ___ after every meal.
explanation: Reflexive: the cat cleans ITSELF (the object is the same as the subject).

sentence: We organised the trip ___.
She should be ashamed of ___ for saying that.
The house ___ is lovely, but the garden is tiny.
explanation: Noun + itself emphasises the noun: the house itself.

sentence: They built the cabin ___.
It was ___ a boring lecture that people walked out.
explanation: such (+a) + adjective + noun + that… — emphasis structure.

sentence: It was ___ dull a lecture that people walked out.
explanation: so + adjective (+a + noun) + that… — the alternative emphatic pattern.

sentence: There were so ___ complaints that the scheme was dropped.
There was so ___ confusion that the event was abandoned.
The letter was written ___ hand, not typed.
hint: written ___ hand = by typewriter or pen?
explanation: 'Written by hand' = handwritten; 'by' names the means.

sentence: He was accused ___ stealing the confidential documents.
explanation: 'Accuse somebody of doing something' — the preposition is fixed.

sentence: It's the first time I've ___ eaten oysters.
explanation: 'The first time + present perfect + ever' emphasises novelty.

sentence: You'd better hurry, ___ you'll miss the flight.
explanation: 'Otherwise' = if you do not, then this will happen.

sentence: The bridge is ___ repair, so traffic uses the bypass.
She made the cake ___, without any help at all.
explanation: 'She made it herself' — the reflexive stresses she did it alone.

sentence: Hardly had we sat down ___ the lights went out.
explanation: 'Hardly … when' is the fixed pair; 'than' belongs to 'no sooner'.

sentence: By this time tomorrow, we ___ have finished the whole report.
explanation: 'By + future time' calls for the future perfect: will have finished.

sentence: The more you practise, ___ easier it becomes.
explanation: 'The more … the easier …' — both halves take 'the'.

sentence: He talks as if he ___ the owner of the place.
explanation: 'As if he were' — subjunctive for an unreal comparison.

sentence: ___ of the two passwords works — try the other one.
hint: not one and not the other
explanation: 'Neither of the two' = not either of them.

sentence: It was ___ a lovely evening that nobody wanted to leave.
explanation: 'Such a lovely evening that …' — 'so' would go directly before an adjective.

sentence: I wish it ___ stop raining.
explanation: 'Wish + would' complains about something you want to stop or change.

sentence: She denied ___ the last piece of cake.
The window has ___ been repaired, I'm glad to say.
explanation: 'Has since been repaired' = between that time and now.

sentence: No matter how hard he pulled, he ___ open the drawer.
There were ___ many customers for the staff to serve properly.
explanation: 'Too many … to …' — excess preventing an outcome.

sentence: The committee meets ___ other month, always on a Tuesday.
explanation: 'Every other month' = one month yes, one month no.

sentence: It was not ___ midnight that the results were announced.
He'd rather cook at home tonight, ___ he?
explanation: The tag repeats the auxiliary: would → wouldn't.

sentence: The museum charges for entry; ___, under-twenties visit free.
explanation: 'However' marks the contrast between paying and free.

sentence: The plane took ___ despite the thick fog.
She was ___ the impression that the interview was today.
explanation: 'Under the impression that …' = believing, perhaps wrongly.

sentence: They marched through the capital ___ protest.
explanation: 'In protest' = as a way of protesting.

sentence: The findings will be published in ___ course.
hint: in ___ course = at the right time
explanation: 'In due course' = eventually, when the time is right.

sentence: ___ further delay, the doors opened and we went in.
I couldn't reach the shelf, ___ how tall I am.
___ being nervous, she delivered a flawless speech.
The report needs ___ before Friday, doesn't it?
___ the whole, the trip was a great success.
The project ran ___ of money halfway through.
explanation: 'Run out of' = use up the supply.
